title: Beef with potatoes, vegetables and cheese sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of tender beef, roasted potatoes and a mix of vegetables – carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale). All of it is covered with a rich cheese sauce that adds a creamy flavor and aroma. Perfect as a hearty lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is a great source of iron, which is better absorbed when paired with vitamin C found in broccoli.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables; baking them with the skin retains most nutrients.
Carrots contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, essential for vision.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables like spinach and kale are among the most concentrated sources of vitamins K, C and folate.
Cheese sauce is often made from butter, flour and milk, with grated cheese added for extra flavor.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete set of essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Iron from beef supports hemoglobin levels and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Broccoli, carrots and leafy greens supply vitamins A, C, K and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes deliver slowly digestible carbs that provide sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: Calcium from cheese sauce
items.content: The cheese sauce adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cheese sauce and fatty cuts of beef can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty; people monitoring blood pressure should watch their salt intake.

items.title: Milk allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: The cheese sauce may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to dairy or intolerant to lactose.

items.title: Potential pathogens in beef
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor bacteria; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the beef, cutting potatoes into wedges or cubes, and lightly sautéing or steaming the vegetables. Drizzle everything with cheese sauce and garnish with fresh herbs if desired. It pairs well with whole‑grain bread or rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For freezing, place in a freezer‑safe bag and use within 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to at least 75 °C (165 °F) before serving.
